record.one_liner: Firecrawl is an API that searches, scrapes, crawls and maps websites and returns clean Markdown or structured JSON for use by LLMs and agents.
record.auth_notes: The REST API takes an API key in the header `Authorization: Bearer $FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`, and the docs describe the key as optional, needed for higher limits. The hosted MCP server also offers a browser sign-in OAuth flow at /v2/mcp-oauth. I did not find a documented OAuth flow for third-party apps calling the REST API, so OAuth2 applies to the MCP server only.
record.access_notes: The free plan gives 1,000 credits per month with no credit card. Limits are 10 requests per minute on scrape, map and search, 2 per minute on crawl, agent and interact, and 2 concurrent requests. The Hobby plan is $19 per month for 5,000 credits. The intro page says some calls work without any key, within limits.
record.blocker: The free tier is small (1,000 credits per month, 10 requests per minute), so real use needs a paid plan. Auth is a static API key, not per-user OAuth for the REST API. I saw only 4 endpoint paths on the intro page (scrape, search, interact create and delete). Map, crawl, agent, parse and webhooks are listed but I did not fetch their reference pages. The "WebSocket" API type is not confirmed by any page I fetched; I listed it from background knowledge, so treat it as unverified.
